title: Six a week
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: Monday, week five. The grid: six dailies and a Sunday. The strip draws its own week as a calendar on the wall with seven boxes and Wood filling the sixth, Saturday, for the first time since 1999.

panels.composition: The bedroom. A calendar page on the wall: a week, seven boxes. Six with a small strip drawn in each. Sunday's box: a smear of color. WOOD at the desk.
props: a calendar with strips in the boxes

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man at a desk beneath a wall calendar whose seven daily boxes each hold a tiny drawn comic strip and the Sunday box holds a smear of watercolor

panels.composition: Saturday's box. The strip in it: the first Saturday since June 1999.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a calendar's Saturday box with a tiny four-panel strip drawn inside it
image.notes: Saturday: the newspaper cadence. Six and a Sunday.

panels.composition: Wood drawing Saturday's. The dog on the bed. The desk, the CRT, the pad, all at once: the machine of it.
props: the desk, the CRT, the pad

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man drawing at a cluttered desk with a CRT and a pad, a small dog on the bed, the whole apparatus visible

panels.composition: The calendar, full. Seven boxes. Wood looking at it the way he looked at the empty frames in 2000. Something to fill every week for seventeen years.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man looking at a full wall calendar of tiny drawn strips, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor

notes: Seven boxes. Saturday for the first time since 1999.
